data.name: Gardener
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, the name Gardener is derived from the Greek word 'georgos', which means 'earth-worker'. The name carries a deep connection to nature and the cultivation of life. Gardener was also a title given to the goddess Demeter, who was the goddess of agriculture and the harvest.

in_greek.name: Κηπουρός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Κηπουρός είναι όρος που περιγράφει τον φύλακα ή τον εργάτη του κήπου. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο όρος σχετίζεται με την εικόνα του Θεού ως του κηπουρού της δημιουργίας.

in_latin.name: Hortulanus
in_latin.long_meaning: Hortulanus est nomen quod describit custodem vel operarium horti. In ecclesia primitiva, nomen refertur ad imaginem Dei ut hortulani creationis.

in_english.name: Gardener
in_english.meaning: one who tends or cultivates a garden
in_english.long_meaning: The name Gardener originates from the Old English words 'geard' meaning 'enclosure' and 'nere' meaning 'keeper'. It refers to one who tends or cultivates a garden. In Christian tradition, the name symbolizes the caretaker of creation, reflecting God's role as the ultimate gardener of Eden. Historically, the name has been associated with Saint Joseph, the husband of Mary, often depicted as a gardener or carpenter.
